title: Training Job Placement in Clusters with Statistical In-Network Aggregation
problem: Job placement in clusters with statistical in-network aggregation must efficiently allocate shared switch memory and balance computation and network resources, as the multiplexed use of switch buffers for gradient aggregation creates cross-layer resource bottlenecks.
motivation: Statistical in-network aggregation improves switch memory utilization and operational simplicity, but requires intelligent job placement to maximize both computation and network resource efficiency in distributed training clusters.
method: NetPack schedules training jobs repeatedly in batches using three components: first, it measures which cluster resources are currently available; second, it scores each server based on its spare GPU capacity and network bandwidth; and third, it applies a dynamic programming algorithm to optimally match each job to its best-fitting server.
key_novelty: NetPack jointly optimizes computing and networking resources during job placement using dynamic programming, specifically designed for clusters where gradient data is aggregated in network switches rather than servers.
contributions: NetPack system for job placement in statistical INA clusters
Steady state estimation algorithm for cluster resource discovery
Heuristic server valuation based on GPU and bandwidth resources
Dynamic programming algorithm for efficient job placement

metrics.speedup: 45% reduction in average job completion time

limitations: Limitations and scalability constraints of statistical multiplexing approach under varying cluster sizes and heterogeneous workloads not discussed.
primary_theme: Job placement optimization for statistical in-network aggregation
